text:
maya: quick triage — customer Cypress reported weird numeric drift after grafting their LoRA into our 7b-int3 variant. Small repro attached.

maya: repro cmd: `rwi serve --model redwood/7b-int3 --patch cypress-lora-v2 && curl -sS localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"Invoice total: $", "max_tokens":10}'`

maya: output sample: `Invoice total: $ 1,200.00` -> expected `1,200.00` but we saw `12,00.00` and also extra commas sometimes. Looks like tokenization/merge alignment issue after quant.

samir: hmm, could be token boundary shift from the LoRA merge + int3 quant kernels. Do we have a quick eval pack run? :thinking_face:

maya: I kicked off an eval-pack (mini) earlier: id eval-1771239999-mini. It ran on single seed, 50 examples (invoices+amounts).

zhen: paste from eval-bot: 
```
EVAL eval-1771239999-mini
model: redwood/7b-int3 + cypress-lora-v2 (graft)
metrics: amount-exact-match: 82/100
token-drop: 0.08 mean shift
notable: comma-placement errors concentrated on numbers with thousands separator
```

oliver: 82% is rough but not catastrophic. Is baseline (without LoRA) at ~98%?

zhen: baseline eval (7b-int3 w/o LoRA) was 97/100 on same mini set. So delta ~15 points.

samir: that delta screams merge-merge aliasing. Two quick checks: 1) tokeniser mapping differences (merge might have changed token ids for digits/comma), 2) KV cache alignment when using graft vs stitch.

maya: i diffed vocab mapping after graft — nothing obvious, but the LoRA introduces new embeddings that shift logit distributions for tokens like `,` and digits.

oliver: can you run a deterministic beam decode on a few failing examples and paste raw logits for the numeric tokens? E.g., set temperature=0, top_k=1 and logprobs=20.

maya: on it. running: `rwi eval --model redwood/7b-int3+patch:cypress-lora-v2 --logprobs 20 --examples failing_ids.txt`

zhen: eval-bot posted results: 
```
EXAMPLE id: cyp-045
prompt: "Invoice total: $"
gold: "1200.00"
decode(t0): tokens: ["1","200",".","00"] logits(top5): [ {"1": -0.2, ",": -0.25, "12": -1.8 }, ... ]
issue: comma token gets higher prob than expected at step 2 -> produces `1,200` vs `1200` parsing mismatch in postproc
```

samir: interesting — the comma token higher prob suggests LoRA nudged scoring. Could be quantization amplifying small shifts. Two-pronged: (A) re-run merge but with post-quant calibration (O2) and (B) try stitch (warm-start) merge instead of graft to preserve token logits.

oliver: also check tokenization detokenize roundtrip for locale settings. Cypress uses en_US invoices with `,` as thousands sep. Rarely we see models learn to insert zero-width spaces or unexpected separators during merge.

maya: trying (A) now: rebake patch with quant-calib and run mini eval. ETA ~15m.

zhen: while that's running, I can assemble a focused eval pack of 500 invoice examples (mix of locales) and run on both graft vs stitch vs baseline. Will take ~2h on a single GPU.

maya: rebake done. quick-run summary from eval-bot: 
```
EVAL eval-1771239999-rebake
redwood/7b-int3+patch:cypress-lora-v2 (rebake+calib): amount-exact-match: 93/100
notes: comma-placement fixed in most cases, small residual on Korean style separators
```

oliver: nice improvement -> suggests quant-calib helps. Still want stitch run to compare.

samir: OK plan: zhen runs 500-example pack across three variants (baseline, graft-rebake, stitch). zhen pls tag results with seed+decode settings. Maya to coordinate customer-facing notes (what changed + recommended deploy path: rebake pipeline + regression check).

maya: noted. I'll draft a short customer message: "We've reproduced the numeric formatting drift after LoRA grafting into int3. Root cause: small logit shifts amplified by quantization leading to comma-token preference. Remediation: rebake + quant calibration or use stitch merge. We're running full eval pack and will share numbers + recommended pipeline."

zhen: started long-run: job eval-1771239999-full (500 ex), queue pos 2. I'll post results here when done.

eval-bot: queued eval-1771239999-full on gpu-4; est runtime ~110m. :robot_face:

oliver: thanks all — good triage. If full eval still shows >5pt regression vs baseline on business-critical parsers, we'll target a hotfix that forces comma-digit token alignment in postproc for Cypress locale as a short-term mitigation.

maya: agreed. tagging @support/cypress for heads-up. :white_check_mark:
